zh: 杜伦大学 为一所坐落于英国东北英格兰城市杜伦的公立研究型大学. 于1832年通过国会法案正式成立，1837年被授予皇家宪章. 是英格兰地区继剑桥大学和牛津大学成立600余年后首间被认可成立的大学，普遍被认为是英格兰第三古老的大学. 杜伦大学为学院制大学，其与剑桥大学和牛津大学为英国仅存的三所中世纪学院制大学，因此在英国三校常被并称为“Doxbridge”.

学术方面，杜伦大学为英国罗素大学集团成员，在英国国内稳定排名前5位，2021年《卫报》将其排名为英国第4位. 以高中生的入学成绩来看，杜伦大学2019年的平均UCAS成绩为195分 ，在全国名列第5，为英国入学门槛最高的大学之一. 国际排名上，2025年位居QS世界大学排名全球89位 ，其中神学与宗教 (7)、古典学与历史 (6) 以及考古学 (5) 位居世界前10名. 《泰晤士报》曾描述，“长久以来，杜伦大学是除了牛津大学和剑桥大学之外最好的选择”，并吸引了“大量来自中产阶级和更富有家庭的学生”.

校园生活方面，杜伦大学实行学院制，目前有17所学院. 不同于教学研究组织，各学院负责社交、娱乐及居住等职能，扮演学生校园生活的重要角色. 每个学院高度自治，有著代表性的院徽、院服、格言、代表色和运动队伍，并有独立的图书馆、体育场、运动设施、教堂、酒吧和食堂，部分学院会固定举行正式晚宴，需穿著黑袍参与. 另外，杜伦大学学生的运动参与率达92% ，长久以来高居英国大学之冠. 校内共有52种不同项目的体育社团，并设置一系列体育设施，包括英国仅有的世界标准规格击剑场，以及英国唯三的室内划船池，板球、英式橄榄球、曲棍球及女子足球等项目也均有多位奥运代表选手及全国冠军纪录.
杜伦大学的现任校监是前美国国家安全会议（欧盟及俄罗斯）高级总监教授担任，当前名誉学者包括14位皇家学会会员、17位英国国家学术院院士、14位社会科学术院院士、爱丁堡皇家学会的5位研究员、皇家文艺学会2名研究员和英国医学科学院2名研究员. 杜伦大学的毕业生会在自己的名字后面加注“Dunelm”（这是Durham的拉丁文缩写）来表示自己毕业于这所大学，视其为荣誉.

在1286~1291年之间，杜伦的本笃会修士在牛津大学建立了一栋大楼，作为学习的场所. 1381年，时任杜伦大主教汤玛士·哈特菲尔德 (Thomas Hatfield) 捐赠了一笔钱，成立杜伦学院 (Durham College). 杜伦悠久的神学教学使人们想在市内建立大学，时任英皇亨利八世和奥立佛·克伦威尔，于1657年发表专利特许证并提名监理和研究员以建立大学. 但是，牛津大学和剑桥大学忧虑授予学位权力可能会影响他们的地位. 因此直到1832年，国会才在查尔斯·索普 (Charles Thorp) 副主教的发起以及时任杜伦大主教威廉·范·米尔德特的支持下，通过了一项法案，许可杜伦大座堂得以部分教会财产建立大学之提案，杜伦大学因此而生，该法案于1832年7月4日获得时任时任英皇威廉四世的御准.
en: The University of Durham, which operates under the trading name of Durham University, is a collegiate public research university in Durham, England, founded by an Act of Parliament in 1832 and incorporated by royal charter in 1837. It was the first recognised university to open in England for more than 600 years, after Oxford and Cambridge, and is thus the third-oldest university in England. As a collegiate university, its main functions are divided between the academic departments of the university and its 17 colleges. In general, the departments perform research and provide teaching to students, while the colleges are responsible for their domestic arrangements and welfare.

The university is a member of the Russell Group of British research universities and is also affiliated with the regional N8 Research Partnership and international university groups including the Matariki Network of Universities and the Coimbra Group. The university estate includes 83 listed buildings, ranging from the 11th-century Durham Castle to the 1960s brutalist students' union. The university also owns and manages the Durham World Heritage Site in partnership with Durham Cathedral. The university's ownership of the world heritage site includes Durham Castle, Palace Green and the surrounding buildings including the historic Cosin's Library.
Durham graduates have long used the Latin post-nominal letters Dunelm after their degree, from Dunelmensis (of, belonging to, or from Durham).

Between around 1286 and 1291 the Benedictine monks of Durham established a hall at the University of Oxford to provide them with a seat of learning. In 1381, the hall received an endowment from Thomas Hatfield, Bishop of Durham, becoming Durham College. Durham College was surrendered to the Crown in 1545 following the Reformation. The strong tradition of theological teaching in Durham gave rise to various attempts to form a university within the city itself, notably under King Henry VIII and then under Oliver Cromwell, who issued letters patent and nominated a proctor and fellows for the establishment of a college in 1657. However, a proposal to allow the college to confer degrees met with opposition from Oxford and Cambridge universities, and the whole scheme was abandoned at the restoration of the monarchy in 1660. Consequently, it was not until 1832 when Parliament, at the instigation of Archdeacon Charles Thorp and with the support of the Bishop of Durham, William van Mildert, passed "an Act to enable the Dean and Chapter of Durham Cathedral to appropriate part of the property of their church to the establishment of a University in connection therewith" (2 & 3 Will. 4. c. 19) that the university came into being. The act received royal assent from King William IV on 4 July 1832.

The university opened on 28 October 1833. In 1834 all but two of the bishops of the Church of England confirmed that they would accept holders of Durham degrees for ordination. In 1835 a fundamental statute was passed by the Dean and Chapter, as governors of the university, setting up Convocation and laying down that Durham degrees would only be open to members of the Church of England. Regulations for degrees were finalised in 1836 and the university was incorporated by royal charter granted by William IV on 1 June 1837 as the "Warden, Masters and Scholars of the University of Durham", with the first students graduating a week later. At the opening of the university, accommodation was provided in the Archdeacon's Inn (now Cosin's Hall); in 1837 an order of the Queen-in-Council was issued granting the university use of Durham Castle, which had previously been a palace of the Bishop of Durham, for further accommodation.
